newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 27.

text.p: Following are the highlights of
Irish press on Friday.
THE IRISH TIMES
- The IRA is believed to have been responsible for a rocket
attack on a police landrover near a sectarian flashpoint in north Belfast last night.
- New Irish prime minister Bertie Ahern is being challenged on the legality of the responsibilities allocated to David Andrews following the appointment of a predictable cabinet late last night.
- Military and police operations to counter widespread loyalist disruption are being prepared in anticipation of a breakdown in talks which begin today to try to avert another Drumcree standoff.
- Talks to resolve the Irish Life sales staff strike are to
resume this morning.
- Electronics multinational Intel received more than 26 million
punts in IDA Ireland grants last year, new figures have shown.
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- Bertie Ahern settled in last night for a long spell as prime
minister after his minority government secured the support of
three committed independent legislators.
- Ireland's youngest prime minister Bertie Ahern plumped for the
'old reliables' in his cabinet, dropping just one member of his
front bench.
- Republican terrorists were blamed for launching a grenade
attack late last night on a police patrol in North Belfast.
- Dawn Meats, accounting for some 15 percent of the Irish
national beef kill, has made a bid for the meat business of the
publicly-quoted Sims Group in the UK.
